newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent, NYMEX rebound after API.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent, NYMEX rebound after API.

text.p: Crude futures rebounded in Asia time on Wednesday, spurred higher by revised stock data that showed a bigger draw in crude stocks than had been previously reported.
February Brent futures, trading on SIMEX, last traded at $23.51 per barrel, up 15 cents from London. March traded at $23.15, up 17 cents from London.
February NYMEX crude futures, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system, last traded at $25.32, up 21 cents from New York.
Both contracts fell overnight on expectations API data would show a sharp rise in crude and gasoline stocks.

In fact, the data showed a rise in crude stocks of 4.65 million barrels -- double expectations -- but the previous week's data was revised to show a fall in stocks of 10.785 million barrels instead of the originally reported 9.47 million.
Gasoline stocks rose just 415,000 barrels, widening the shortfall versus a year earlier and indicating it would be difficult to rebuild stocks in time for the driving season.
NYMEX products rebounded with the API data.
February heating oil last traded 0.78 cent higher than New York at 70.20 cents per gallon, and gasoline regained 0.56 of New York's 1.05 loss to last trade at 67.60.
